paragraphs.text: הַחֲרִ֤ישׁוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֔ים וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ יִגְּשׁוּ֙ אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ יַחְדָּ֖ו לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט נִקְרָֽבָה׃

i18n.en: Keep silence before me, O coastlands, and let the peoples renew their strength; let them draw near, then let them speak; let us come near together to judgment.
i18n.he: הַחֲרִ֤ישׁוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֔ים וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ יִגְּשׁוּ֙ אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ יַחְדָּ֖ו לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט נִקְרָֽבָה׃

notes.official:
*ʾIyyîm* “coastlands”: *ʾî* is “coast, island, shore, region” (BDB, Sefaria lexicon, checked), the lands on and across the sea, mostly the Mediterranean shores and islands. ASV and JPS 1917 have “islands”, and NJPS has “coastlands” (checked). The line keeps the book's “coastlands” (stable 11:11; 24:15; 40:15; 42:4, 10, 12) under overlay `iy-coastlands-isaiah`, which now gathers the book's *ʾî* sites.

*Ûlᵉʾummîm yaḥălîp̄û ḵōaḥ* “and let the peoples renew their strength” repeats the words of 40:31 (“shall renew their strength”). NJPS keeps the clause but notes “Connection of Heb. uncertain” (checked). Many commentators take it as a copyist's repetition from 40:31 and emend it, for example to a verb of waiting or drawing near; those proposals were not verified here. The line translates MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

The verse opens a trial scene. *Yiggᵉšû ʾāz yᵉḏabbērû yaḥdāw lammišpāṭ niqrāḇāh* is “let them draw near, then let them speak; let us come near together to judgment” (ASV; NJPS “for argument”).

paragraphs.text: מִ֤י הֵעִיר֙ מִמִּזְרָ֔ח צֶ֖דֶק יִקְרָאֵ֣הוּ לְרַגְל֑וֹ יִתֵּ֨ן לְפָנָ֤יו גּוֹיִם֙ וּמְלָכִ֣ים יַ֔רְדְּ יִתֵּ֤ן כֶּֽעָפָר֙ חַרְבּ֔וֹ כְּקַ֥שׁ נִדָּ֖ף קַשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Who has roused one from the east, whom he calls in righteousness to his foot? He gives nations before him, and makes him rule over kings; he makes them like dust to his sword, like driven stubble to his bow.
i18n.he: מִ֤י הֵעִיר֙ מִמִּזְרָ֔ח צֶ֖דֶק יִקְרָאֵ֣הוּ לְרַגְל֑וֹ יִתֵּ֨ן לְפָנָ֤יו גּוֹיִם֙ וּמְלָכִ֣ים יַ֔רְדְּ יִתֵּ֤ן כֶּֽעָפָר֙ חַרְבּ֔וֹ כְּקַ֥שׁ נִדָּ֖ף קַשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

notes.official:
*Mî hēʿîr mimmizrāḥ* “Who has roused one from the east”: the same verb is used of the same figure at 41:25 (*haʿîrôṯî*) and 45:13 (*haʿîrōṯihû* “I have roused him”). The line therefore has “roused”, as the stable 45:13 and NJPS do, where ASV has “raised up” (checked). The Hebrew names no one here. Most commentators identify the figure with Cyrus, who is named at 44:28 and 45:1. The line leaves the figure unnamed and in lower case.

*Ṣeḏeq yiqrāʾēhû lᵉraḡlô* has no preposition before *ṣeḏeq*. ASV takes the noun adverbially, “whom he calleth in righteousness to his foot”; the stable 42:6 and 45:13 have the same idea with the preposition (*bᵉṣeḏeq*, “in righteousness”). JPS 1917 makes *ṣeḏeq* the subject, “At whose steps victory attendeth”. NJPS reads a concrete noun, “roused a victor … Summoned him to His service”, with the note “Lit. ‘victory’” (all checked). The line keeps ASV. *Lᵉraḡlô* “to his foot” means “to follow him, into his service”.

*Ûmᵉlāḵîm yard* “and makes him rule over kings” reads *yard* as a short form from *rādāh* “rule”, with ASV and JPS 1917. NJPS has “And trodden sovereigns down” (checked), which gives the verb the sense “tread down”. A derivation from *yārad* “bring down”, said to be supported by 1QIsaᵃ, was not verified. In *yittēn keʿāp̄ār ḥarbô* “he makes them like dust to his sword” (ASV), NJPS takes the suffixes as the enemies' weapons, “Has rendered their swords like dust”, noting “Heb. ‘his’” (checked).

paragraphs.text: יִרְדְּפֵ֖ם יַעֲב֣וֹר שָׁל֑וֹם אֹ֥רַח בְּרַגְלָ֖יו לֹ֥א יָבֽוֹא׃

i18n.en: He pursues them and passes on safely, by a path that he has not gone with his feet.
i18n.he: יִרְדְּפֵ֖ם יַעֲב֣וֹר שָׁל֑וֹם אֹ֥רַח בְּרַגְלָ֖יו לֹ֥א יָבֽוֹא׃

notes.official: *ʾŌraḥ bᵉraḡlāyw lōʾ yāḇôʾ* is uncertain. ASV has “by a way that he had not gone with his feet”, an unfamiliar road. JPS 1917 has “The way with his feet he treadeth not”, of speed. NJPS has “No shackle is placed on his feet”, with the note that *ʾrḥ* has this meaning in Old Aramaic (all checked). The line keeps ASV in the present tense. *Šālôm* is adverbial, “safely” (ASV; NJPS “unscathed”).

paragraphs.text: מִֽי־פָעַ֣ל וְעָשָׂ֔ה קֹרֵ֥א הַדֹּר֖וֹת מֵרֹ֑אשׁ אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ רִאשׁ֔וֹן וְאֶת־אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים אֲנִי־הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: Who has acted and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, YHWH, am the first, and with the last I am he.
i18n.he: מִֽי־פָעַ֣ל וְעָשָׂ֔ה קֹרֵ֥א הַדֹּר֖וֹת מֵרֹ֑אשׁ אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ רִאשׁ֔וֹן וְאֶת־אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים אֲנִי־הֽוּא׃

notes.official:
*Mî-p̄āʿal wᵉʿāśāh* “Who has acted and done it”: *pāʿal* is “act”, as in the stable 43:13 (“I act”), where ASV has “wrought”. *ʿĀśāh* here means “do”, so the central `asah` (“made”) is not applied. *Qōrēʾ haddōrôṯ mērōʾš* “calling the generations from the beginning” follows ASV; JPS 1917 and NJPS make it the answer to the question, “He that called …” and “He who announced the generations from the start” (checked).

*ʾĂnî YHWH rišôn wᵉʾeṯ-ʾaḥărōnîm ʾănî-hûʾ* has no verb. ASV keeps it verbless: “I, Jehovah, the first, and with the last, I am he”. JPS 1917 has “who am the first, And with the last am the same”, and NJPS “who was first And will be with the last as well” (checked). The line supplies “am” to match the stable 44:6 (“I am the first and I am the last”) and 48:12 (“I am he; I am the first”). It keeps the plural *ʾaḥărōnîm* as “with the last” and the closing *ʾănî-hûʾ* as “I am he”, the formula of 43:10, 13 and 48:12.

paragraphs.text: רָא֤וּ אִיִּים֙ וְיִירָ֔אוּ קְצ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ קָרְב֖וּ וַיֶּאֱתָיֽוּן׃

i18n.en: The coastlands have seen and are afraid; the ends of the earth tremble; they have drawn near and come.
i18n.he: רָא֤וּ אִיִּים֙ וְיִירָ֔אוּ קְצ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ קָרְב֖וּ וַיֶּאֱתָיֽוּן׃

notes.official: *Rāʾû ʾiyyîm wᵉyîrāʾû* “The coastlands have seen and are afraid” (overlay `iy-coastlands-isaiah`; ASV and JPS 1917 “The isles”, NJPS “The coastlands”, checked). *Qᵉṣôṯ hāʾāreṣ* “the ends of the earth” is the book's universal idiom (overlay `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24`).

paragraphs.text: אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֖הוּ יַעְזֹ֑רוּ וּלְאָחִ֖יו יֹאמַ֥ר חֲזָֽק׃

i18n.en: They help everyone his neighbor, and everyone says to his brother, “Be strong!”
i18n.he: אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֖הוּ יַעְזֹ֑רוּ וּלְאָחִ֖יו יֹאמַ֥ר חֲזָֽק׃

notes.official:
*ʾÎš ʾeṯ-rēʿēhû yaʿzōrû ûlᵉʾāḥîw yōʾmar* “They help everyone his neighbor, and everyone says to his brother”: distributive *ʾîš* is “everyone” (overlay `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah`). The singular suffixes stay “his” under the house rule that keeps he/his after a gender-neutral noun, as in the stable 19:2 (“everyone against his brother”). ASV has “every one his neighbor … [every one] saith to his brother”, and NJPS “Each one helps the other, Saying to his fellow” (checked). *Ḥăzāq* “Be strong!” is the imperative rendered so at 35:4 (*ḥizqû*); ASV and JPS 1917 have “Be of good courage”, and NJPS “Take courage!”

The root *ḥzq* runs through the chapter in several senses, and the line renders each by context: “Be strong” (41:6), “encourages” and “fastens it” (41:7), “taken hold of” (41:9; cf. 42:6), and “grasp your right hand” (41:13; cf. 45:1). The repetition sets the craftsmen's work on the idol (41:6–7) beside YHWH's hold on Israel (41:9, 13). A single English verb would force at least one of these senses.

paragraphs.text: וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק חָרָשׁ֙ אֶת־צֹרֵ֔ף מַחֲלִ֥יק פַּטִּ֖ישׁ אֶת־ה֣וֹלֶם פָּ֑עַם אֹמֵ֤ר לַדֶּ֙בֶק֙ ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַיְחַזְּקֵ֥הוּ בְמַסְמְרִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט׃ (ס)

i18n.en: So the craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and the one who smooths with the hammer the one who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, “It is good”; and he fastens it with nails, so that it will not totter.
i18n.he: וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק חָרָשׁ֙ אֶת־צֹרֵ֔ף מַחֲלִ֥יק פַּטִּ֖ישׁ אֶת־ה֣וֹלֶם פָּ֑עַם אֹמֵ֤ר לַדֶּ֙בֶק֙ ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַיְחַזְּקֵ֥הוּ בְמַסְמְרִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט׃ (ס)

notes.official: The craft vocabulary follows the stable 40:19–20. *Ḥārāš* is “craftsman” and *ṣōrēp̄* “goldsmith” (ASV and JPS 1917 “the carpenter … the goldsmith”; NJPS “The woodworker … the smith”). *Lōʾ yimmôṭ* is “will not totter”, as at 40:20 (ASV “should not be moved”; NJPS “may not topple”). *Hôlem pāʿam* “the one who strikes the anvil” follows ASV and JPS 1917 (NJPS “him who pounds the anvil”); *paʿam* is usually “step, time”, and “anvil” is the contextual sense. *Laddeḇeq* is “of the soldering” (ASV, JPS 1917), and NJPS has “of the riveting” (all checked).

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדִּ֔י יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ זֶ֖רַע אַבְרָהָ֥ם אֹהֲבִֽי׃

i18n.en: But you, Israel my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend,
i18n.he: וְאַתָּה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדִּ֔י יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ זֶ֖רַע אַבְרָהָ֥ם אֹהֲבִֽי׃

notes.official:
*Zeraʿ ʾaḇrāhām ʾōhăḇî* “the seed of Abraham my friend”: *zeraʿ* is “seed” in the stable chapters (43:5; 44:3; 45:19, 25; 48:19), where “offspring” renders a different noun, *ṣeʾĕṣāʾîm* (44:3; 48:19). ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all have “seed” here (checked). *ʾŌhăḇî* is the active participle with a suffix, literally “the one who loves me”. ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS have “my friend” (checked), and 2 Chr 20:7 calls Abraham *ʾōhaḇḵā* “your friend” with the same participle (MT checked). Jas 2:23 takes up the title (recalled, not verified).

*Yiśrāʾēl ʿaḇdî* “Israel my servant”: here the servant is named as Israel and Jacob, as at 44:1–2, 21 and 45:4 (overlay `eved-servant-identity-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶחֱזַקְתִּ֙יךָ֙ מִקְצ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵאֲצִילֶ֖יהָ קְרָאתִ֑יךָ וָאֹ֤מַר לְךָ֙ עַבְדִּי־אַ֔תָּה בְּחַרְתִּ֖יךָ וְלֹ֥א מְאַסְתִּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: you whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, “You are my servant; I have chosen you and not rejected you”:
i18n.he: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶחֱזַקְתִּ֙יךָ֙ מִקְצ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵאֲצִילֶ֖יהָ קְרָאתִ֑יךָ וָאֹ֤מַר לְךָ֙ עַבְדִּי־אַ֔תָּה בְּחַרְתִּ֖יךָ וְלֹ֥א מְאַסְתִּֽיךָ׃

notes.official: *Heḥĕzaqtîḵā* “I have taken hold of” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “drew”); cf. 42:6, “I will take hold of your hand”. *Mēʾăṣîleyhā* is “from its corners” (ASV “the corners thereof”; NJPS “its far corners”). *Mᵉʾastîḵā* is “rejected”, with NJPS, for ASV and JPS 1917 “cast thee away” (checked). The quotation “You are my servant; I have chosen you and not rejected you” has the extent that JPS 1917 marks (overlay `eved-servant-identity-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י עִמְּךָ־אָ֔נִי אַל־תִּשְׁתָּ֖ע כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אִמַּצְתִּ֙יךָ֙ אַף־עֲזַרְתִּ֔יךָ אַף־תְּמַכְתִּ֖יךָ בִּימִ֥ין צִדְקִֽי׃

i18n.en: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, yes, I will help you, yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
i18n.he: אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י עִמְּךָ־אָ֔נִי אַל־תִּשְׁתָּ֖ע כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אִמַּצְתִּ֙יךָ֙ אַף־עֲזַרְתִּ֔יךָ אַף־תְּמַכְתִּ֖יךָ בִּימִ֥ין צִדְקִֽי׃

notes.official:
*ʾAl-tîrāʾ kî ʿimmᵉḵā-ʾānî* “Do not fear, for I am with you” is the formula of the central `al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`, whose rationale names this verse. The line has the entry's wording exactly. The opener recurs without the presence clause at 41:13–14, 43:1 and 44:2, and with it at 43:5. *ʾAl-tištāʿ* “do not be dismayed” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “Be not frightened”) is the verb of *wᵉništāʿāh* at 41:23. *ʾĂnî ʾĕlōheyḵā* is “I am your God” (overlay `elohai-elohenu-doxology-isaiah-25`).

The three suffixed perfects *ʾimmaṣtîḵā ʾap̄-ʿăzartîḵā ʾap̄-tᵉmaḵtîḵā* are rendered as futures with ASV: “I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee”. JPS 1917 and NJPS render them as presents, “I strengthen thee, yea, I help thee” and “I strengthen you and I help you” (checked). Both renderings treat the perfect as the assurance of the oracle. The line keeps ASV, and the same choice governs *ʿăzartîḵā* at 41:13 and 41:14 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`). *Bîmîn ṣiḏqî* is “with the right hand of my righteousness” (ASV). JPS 1917 and NJPS have “with My victorious right hand”, giving *ṣeḏeq* the sense “victory”, as NJPS also does at 41:2.

paragraphs.text: הֵ֤ן יֵבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ וְיִכָּ֣לְמ֔וּ כֹּ֖ל הַנֶּחֱרִ֣ים בָּ֑ךְ יִֽהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וְיֹאבְד֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י רִיבֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: Behold, all who are incensed against you shall be put to shame and confounded; those who strive with you shall be as nothing and shall perish.
i18n.he: הֵ֤ן יֵבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ וְיִכָּ֣לְמ֔וּ כֹּ֖ל הַנֶּחֱרִ֣ים בָּ֑ךְ יִֽהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וְיֹאבְד֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י רִיבֶֽךָ׃

notes.official:
*Hēn yēḇōšû wᵉyikkālᵉmû kōl hanneḥĕrîm bāḵ* “all who are incensed against you shall be put to shame and confounded” matches the stable 45:16 (“put to shame and also confounded”) and 45:24 (“all who were incensed against him”).

*ʾAnšê rîḇeḵā* (41:11), *ʾanšê maṣṣuṯeḵā* and *ʾanšê milḥamtᵉḵā* (41:12) are constructs with *ʾănāšîm*, literally “men of your strife … of your contention … of your war”. They name Israel's adversaries in general, not a body of fighters, so the line follows ASV's relative clauses: “those who strive with you … those who contend with you … those who war against you” (overlay `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah`). NJPS has “All who contend with you … They who strive with you” here, and “The men who battle against you” at 41:12 (checked).

paragraphs.text: תְּבַקְשֵׁם֙ וְלֹ֣א תִמְצָאֵ֔ם אַנְשֵׁ֖י מַצֻּתֶ֑ךָ יִהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וּכְאֶ֖פֶס אַנְשֵׁ֥י מִלְחַמְתֶּֽךָ׃

i18n.en: You shall seek them and not find them, those who contend with you; those who war against you shall be as nothing, and as nought.
i18n.he: תְּבַקְשֵׁם֙ וְלֹ֣א תִמְצָאֵ֔ם אַנְשֵׁ֖י מַצֻּתֶ֑ךָ יִהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וּכְאֶ֖פֶס אַנְשֵׁ֥י מִלְחַמְתֶּֽךָ׃

notes.official: *Yihyû ḵᵉʾayin ûḵᵉʾep̄es* “shall be as nothing, and as nought” (ASV “as a thing of nought”; NJPS “Less than nothing”, checked). The chapter's words for nothingness keep the ASV pattern (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`): *ʾayin* is “nothing” (41:11, 12, 24; cf. 40:17), *ʾep̄es* is “nought” (41:12, 29), *ʾāp̄aʿ* is also “nought” (41:24; a word found only there, often read as a form of *ʾep̄es*), *ʾāwen* is “vanity” (41:29), and *tōhû* is “emptiness” (41:29; 40:17, 23). At 40:17 *mēʾep̄es* is the comparative idiom “less than nothing”.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֗י אֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מַחֲזִ֣יק יְמִינֶ֑ךָ הָאֹמֵ֥ר לְךָ֛ אַל־תִּירָ֖א אֲנִ֥י עֲזַרְתִּֽיךָ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For I, YHWH your God, grasp your right hand, saying to you, “Do not fear; I will help you.”
i18n.he: כִּ֗י אֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מַחֲזִ֣יק יְמִינֶ֑ךָ הָאֹמֵ֥ר לְךָ֛ אַל־תִּירָ֖א אֲנִ֥י עֲזַרְתִּֽיךָ׃ (ס)

notes.official: *Maḥăzîq yᵉmîneḵā* “grasp your right hand”: the participle takes the verb of the stable 45:1 (“whose right hand I have grasped”). ASV has “will hold”, JPS 1917 “Hold”, and NJPS “Who grasped” (checked). *Hāʾōmēr lᵉḵā* is “saying to you” (ASV; JPS 1917 “Who say unto thee”). *ʾAl-tîrāʾ ʾănî ʿăzartîḵā* is “Do not fear; I will help you” (central `al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`; tense as at 41:10).

paragraphs.text: אַל־תִּֽירְאִי֙ תּוֹלַ֣עַת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב מְתֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֤י עֲזַרְתִּיךְ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Do not fear, you worm Jacob, you people of Israel! I will help you, says YHWH, and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
i18n.he: אַל־תִּֽירְאִי֙ תּוֹלַ֣עַת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב מְתֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֤י עֲזַרְתִּיךְ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

notes.official:
*Mᵉṯê yiśrāʾēl* “you people of Israel”: *mᵉṯîm* is a plural noun meaning “men”, and ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS have “men of Israel” (checked). BDB lists this verse among the poetic uses in which “sex [is] usually not emph.” (Sefaria lexicon, checked). The phrase addresses the whole people in parallel with “worm Jacob”, and the addressee is grammatically feminine (*ʾal-tîrʾî*, *ʿăzartîḵ*, *gōʾălēḵ*). Under the house rule that generic human nouns are gender-neutral (overlay `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah`), the line has “people”. “Mortal” is kept for *ʾĕnôš* (overlay `enosh-mortal-isaiah`). In prose, *mᵉṯê mispār* means “few in number” (Gen 34:30; Deut 4:27, both so printed in the corpus), and some versions render “you few of Israel”. NJPS notes “Emendation yields ‘maggot’”, which would pair with “worm” (checked). The line translates MT (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`).

*Tôlaʿaṯ yaʿăqōḇ* is “you worm Jacob” (ASV “thou worm Jacob”). *Wᵉgōʾălēḵ qᵉḏôš yiśrāʾēl* “and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel” takes the clause as a predication, with ASV and the stable 54:5. JPS 1917 (“And thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”) and NJPS (“I your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”) read it as apposition (checked), like the formula of 43:14 and 48:17. “Redeemer” is capitalised as a divine title (central `goel-geullah-redeemer-redemption-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֣ה שַׂמְתִּ֗יךְ לְמוֹרַג֙ חָר֣וּץ חָדָ֔שׁ בַּ֖עַל פִּֽיפִיּ֑וֹת תָּד֤וּשׁ הָרִים֙ וְתָדֹ֔ק וּגְבָע֖וֹת כַּמֹּ֥ץ תָּשִֽׂים׃

i18n.en: Behold, I have made you a new, sharp threshing board having teeth; you shall thresh the mountains and crush them, and make the hills like chaff.
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֣ה שַׂמְתִּ֗יךְ לְמוֹרַג֙ חָר֣וּץ חָדָ֔שׁ בַּ֖עַל פִּֽיפִיּ֑וֹת תָּד֤וּשׁ הָרִים֙ וְתָדֹ֔ק וּגְבָע֖וֹת כַּמֹּ֥ץ תָּשִֽׂים׃

notes.official:
*Lᵉmôraḡ ḥārûṣ ḥāḏāš baʿal pîp̄iyyôṯ* “a new, sharp threshing board having teeth”: *môraḡ* is the threshing board, a heavy sledge with stones or iron set in its underside. NJPS has “threshing board” here and at 2 Sam 24:22 (checked); ASV has “threshing instrument”, and JPS 1917 “threshing-sledge”. The line uses “threshing board” because the stable 28:27 already gives “threshing sledge” to *ḥārûṣ* used as a noun. BDB takes *ḥārûṣ* at both sites as one adjective, “sharp”: used with *môraḡ* here and “as subst.” at 28:27 (checked). ASV and JPS 1917 read it as an adjective here too (“new sharp”, “sharp teeth”). NJPS takes *ḥārûṣ ḥāḏāš* as a second noun, “A new thresher” (checked). The central `kalah-venecheratzah-decreed-full-end-cross-corpus`, which covers the *ḥrṣ* of decree, is not applied (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`).

*Baʿal pîp̄iyyôṯ*, literally “owner of edges” or “of mouths”, is “having teeth” (ASV; NJPS “with many spikes”). *Tāḏûš … wᵉṯāḏōq* is “thresh … and crush” (cf. 28:28 “crushed”), and *kammōṣ* is “like chaff”, as at 17:13 and 29:5.

paragraphs.text: תִּזְרֵם֙ וְר֣וּחַ תִּשָּׂאֵ֔ם וּסְעָרָ֖ה תָּפִ֣יץ אוֹתָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל בַּֽיהוָ֔ה בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּתְהַלָּֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: You shall winnow them, and the wind shall carry them off, and the storm shall scatter them; and you shall rejoice in YHWH, you shall glory in the Holy One of Israel.
i18n.he: תִּזְרֵם֙ וְר֣וּחַ תִּשָּׂאֵ֔ם וּסְעָרָ֖ה תָּפִ֣יץ אוֹתָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל בַּֽיהוָ֔ה בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּתְהַלָּֽל׃ (פ)

notes.official: *Tizrēm* “You shall winnow them” (ASV; JPS 1917 “fan”), and *sᵉʿārāh* is “the storm” (ASV and JPS 1917 “the whirlwind”). *Tiṯhallāl* “you shall glory” is the Hithpael of *hll* “praise, boast”, as in the stable 45:25 (“shall glory”); it is not *kāḇôḏ*, the noun the book reserves “glory” for.

paragraphs.text: הָעֲנִיִּ֨ים וְהָאֶבְיוֹנִ֜ים מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים מַ֙יִם֙ וָאַ֔יִן לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם בַּצָּמָ֣א נָשָׁ֑תָּה אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶעֱנֵ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א אֶעֶזְבֵֽם׃

i18n.en: The poor and the needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue is parched with thirst; I, YHWH, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
i18n.he: הָעֲנִיִּ֨ים וְהָאֶבְיוֹנִ֜ים מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים מַ֙יִם֙ וָאַ֔יִן לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם בַּצָּמָ֣א נָשָׁ֑תָּה אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶעֱנֵ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א אֶעֶזְבֵֽם׃

notes.official: *Lᵉšônām baṣṣāmāʾ nāšattāh* “their tongue is parched with thirst” follows NJPS (ASV and JPS 1917 “faileth for thirst”, checked); the verb means “be dry, parched”. *ʾĔlōhê yiśrāʾēl* is “the God of Israel” (overlay `elohei-yisrael-god-of-israel-isaiah-24`).

paragraphs.text: אֶפְתַּ֤ח עַל־שְׁפָיִים֙ נְהָר֔וֹת וּבְת֥וֹךְ בְּקָע֖וֹת מַעְיָנ֑וֹת אָשִׂ֤ים מִדְבָּר֙ לַאֲגַם־מַ֔יִם וְאֶ֥רֶץ צִיָּ֖ה לְמוֹצָ֥אֵי מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the midst of the valleys; I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
i18n.he: אֶפְתַּ֤ח עַל־שְׁפָיִים֙ נְהָר֔וֹת וּבְת֥וֹךְ בְּקָע֖וֹת מַעְיָנ֑וֹת אָשִׂ֤ים מִדְבָּר֙ לַאֲגַם־מַ֔יִם וְאֶ֥רֶץ צִיָּ֖ה לְמוֹצָ֥אֵי מָֽיִם׃

notes.official: *ʾEreṣ ṣiyyāh* “the dry land” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “The arid land”, checked): in parallel with *midbār* “wilderness”, the line keeps the pair of 35:1 (“the wilderness and the dry land”). The stable 53:2 renders *mēʾereṣ ṣiyyāh* as “out of parched ground”, where the phrase names the soil a root grows in; the two renderings stand by context (central `eretz`). *Šᵉp̄āyîm* is “bare heights” (ASV; NJPS “bare hills”), and *ʾăḡam-mayim* “a pool of water” (cf. 35:7).

paragraphs.text: אֶתֵּ֤ן בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֶ֣רֶז שִׁטָּ֔ה וַהֲדַ֖ס וְעֵ֣ץ שָׁ֑מֶן אָשִׂ֣ים בָּעֲרָבָ֗ה בְּר֛וֹשׁ תִּדְהָ֥ר וּתְאַשּׁ֖וּר יַחְדָּֽו׃

i18n.en: I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle, and the oil tree; I will set in the desert the cypress, the pine, and the box tree together,
i18n.he: אֶתֵּ֤ן בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֶ֣רֶז שִׁטָּ֔ה וַהֲדַ֖ס וְעֵ֣ץ שָׁ֑מֶן אָשִׂ֣ים בָּעֲרָבָ֗ה בְּר֛וֹשׁ תִּדְהָ֥ר וּתְאַשּׁ֖וּר יַחְדָּֽו׃

notes.official: The verse names seven trees. *ʾErez* “cedar”, *šiṭṭāh* “acacia” and *hăḏas* “myrtle” are secure. *ʿĒṣ šemen* is “oil tree” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “oleasters”). *Bᵉrôš* is “cypress”, as in the stable 14:8 (ASV “fir-tree”; JPS 1917 and NJPS “cypress”). *Tiḏhār* and *tᵉʾaššûr* are uncertain: ASV has “the pine, and the box-tree”, JPS 1917 “the plane-tree, and the larch”, and NJPS “Box trees and elms” (all checked). The line keeps ASV. *ʿĂrāḇāh* is the common noun “desert”, as at 40:3 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`).

paragraphs.text: לְמַ֧עַן יִרְא֣וּ וְיֵדְע֗וּ וְיָשִׂ֤ימוּ וְיַשְׂכִּ֙ילוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כִּ֥י יַד־יְהוָ֖ה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּ֑את וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּרָאָֽהּ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: that they may see and know, and consider and understand together, that the hand of YHWH has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
i18n.he: לְמַ֧עַן יִרְא֣וּ וְיֵדְע֗וּ וְיָשִׂ֤ימוּ וְיַשְׂכִּ֙ילוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כִּ֥י יַד־יְהוָ֖ה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּ֑את וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּרָאָֽהּ׃ (פ)

notes.official: *Ûqᵉḏôš yiśrāʾēl bᵉrāʾāh* “and the Holy One of Israel has created it” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “has wrought it”, checked; overlay `bara-create-isaiah`). *Wᵉyāśîmû* “and consider” is elliptical for “set (the heart)”, as the full phrase *wᵉnāśîmāh libbēnû* in 41:22 shows.

paragraphs.text: קָרְב֥וּ רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הַגִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ עֲצֻמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם יֹאמַ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: Present your case, says YHWH; bring forward your strong reasons, says the King of Jacob.
i18n.he: קָרְב֥וּ רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הַגִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ עֲצֻמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם יֹאמַ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

notes.official: *Qārᵉḇû rîḇᵉḵem* “Present your case” is literally “bring near your case” (ASV and JPS 1917 “Produce your cause”; NJPS “Submit your case”). *ʿĂṣumôṯêḵem* is “your strong reasons” (ASV; JPS 1917 “your reasons”; NJPS “your pleas”, checked), a rare noun from *ʿṣm* “be strong”. *Meleḵ yaʿăqōḇ* “the King of Jacob” is a divine title and is capitalised (cf. 44:6, “the King of Israel”).

paragraphs.text: יַגִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקְרֶ֑ינָה הָרִאשֹׁנ֣וֹת ׀ מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה הַגִּ֜ידוּ וְנָשִׂ֤ימָה לִבֵּ֙נוּ֙ וְנֵדְעָ֣ה אַחֲרִיתָ֔ן א֥וֹ הַבָּא֖וֹת הַשְׁמִיעֻֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: Let them bring them forward and declare to us what shall happen. The former things, what they were — declare them, that we may consider them and know their end; or make us hear the things to come.
i18n.he: יַגִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקְרֶ֑ינָה הָרִאשֹׁנ֣וֹת ׀ מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה הַגִּ֜ידוּ וְנָשִׂ֤ימָה לִבֵּ֙נוּ֙ וְנֵדְעָ֣ה אַחֲרִיתָ֔ן א֥וֹ הַבָּא֖וֹת הַשְׁמִיעֻֽנוּ׃

notes.official: *Yaggîšû* “Let them bring them forward” takes the Hiphil as transitive, with ASV and JPS 1917. NJPS reads it intransitively, “Let them approach”, with a note (checked). *Hārišōnôṯ* is “the former things” (cf. 42:9; 43:9; 48:3), and *habbāʾôṯ* “the things to come” (ASV, JPS 1917). *Mâ hēnnāh* has no verb (ASV “what they are”); the line supplies the past because the former things are past events, as NJPS does (“what has occurred”). *Hašmîʿunû* is “make us hear”, following 43:9 (ASV “show us”). *ʾAḥărîṯān* is “their end” (JPS 1917 “the end of them”; ASV “the latter end of them”).

paragraphs.text: הַגִּ֙ידוּ֙ הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת לְאָח֔וֹר וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם אַף־תֵּיטִ֣יבוּ וְתָרֵ֔עוּ וְנִשְׁתָּ֖עָה ונרא [וְנִרְאֶ֥ה] יַחְדָּֽו׃

i18n.en: Declare the things that are coming hereafter, that we may know that you are gods; yes, do good or do evil, that we may be dismayed and see it together.
i18n.he: הַגִּ֙ידוּ֙ הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת לְאָח֔וֹר וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם אַף־תֵּיטִ֣יבוּ וְתָרֵ֔עוּ וְנִשְׁתָּ֖עָה ונרא [וְנִרְאֶ֥ה] יַחְדָּֽו׃

notes.official:
*Haggîḏû hāʾōṯiyyôṯ lᵉʾāḥôr* “Declare the things that are coming hereafter”: *hāʾōṯiyyôṯ*, the feminine plural participle of *ʾāṯāh* “come”, is “the things that are coming”, as in the stable 44:7, and *lᵉʾāḥôr* is “hereafter” (ASV and JPS 1917 “the things that are to come hereafter”). The stable 45:11 renders the same participle “the things to come”. The two stable sites differ; this verse follows 44:7, so that *habbāʾôṯ* (41:22) and *hāʾōṯiyyôṯ* keep different English in adjacent verses (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`).

*Kî ʾĕlōhîm ʾattem* “that you are gods”: lower-case “gods” for the idols addressed (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). *ʾAp̄-têṭîḇû wᵉṯārēʿû* “yes, do good or do evil” (ASV; NJPS “Do anything, good or bad”) is a pairing of opposites for any act at all; cf. 45:7, where *rāʿ* is “calamity”.

*Wᵉništāʿāh wᵉnirʾeh yaḥdāw* “that we may be dismayed and see it together”: the written text (ketiv) ונרא can be vocalised *wᵉnîrāʾ* “and fear”, and the reading tradition (qere) is *wᵉnirʾeh* “and see”. The line follows the qere (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`), as ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS do. NJPS notes “Change of vocalization yields ‘fear’; cf. v. 10” (checked). *Wᵉništāʿāh* is taken from *štʿ* “be dismayed”, the verb of 41:10; a derivation from *šʿh* “look (at one another)” has also been proposed (not verified).

paragraphs.text: הֵן־אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן וּפָעָלְכֶ֖ם מֵאָ֑פַע תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה יִבְחַ֥ר בָּכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Behold, you are of nothing, and your work is of nought; an abomination is the one who chooses you.
i18n.he: הֵן־אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן וּפָעָלְכֶ֖ם מֵאָ֑פַע תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה יִבְחַ֥ר בָּכֶֽם׃

notes.official: *Hēn-ʾattem mēʾayin ûp̄āʿolᵉḵem mēʾāp̄aʿ* “you are of nothing, and your work is of nought” (ASV): the preposition *min* can be partitive, “of nothing” (ASV), or comparative, as in NJPS “less than nothing … less than nullity” (checked). *ʾĀp̄aʿ* occurs only here. It is often corrected to *ʾep̄es* (41:12, 29) or linked with *ʾep̄ʿeh* “viper” (30:6); neither proposal was verified. The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`) and shares “nought” with *ʾep̄es* (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`). In *tôʿēḇāh yiḇḥar bāḵem* “an abomination is the one who chooses you”, the relative clause has no relative particle; ASV has “he that chooseth you”, and the line renders it neutrally (central `toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword`).

paragraphs.text: הַעִיר֤וֹתִי מִצָּפוֹן֙ וַיַּ֔את מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ יִקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֑י וְיָבֹ֤א סְגָנִים֙ כְּמוֹ־חֹ֔מֶר וּכְמ֥וֹ יוֹצֵ֖ר יִרְמָס־טִֽיט׃

i18n.en: I have roused one from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun, one who calls on my name; and he shall come upon rulers as upon mortar, and as the potter treads clay.
i18n.he: הַעִיר֤וֹתִי מִצָּפוֹן֙ וַיַּ֔את מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ יִקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֑י וְיָבֹ֤א סְגָנִים֙ כְּמוֹ־חֹ֔מֶר וּכְמ֥וֹ יוֹצֵ֖ר יִרְמָס־טִֽיט׃

notes.official:
*Haʿîrôṯî miṣṣāp̄ôn wayyaʾṯ* “I have roused one from the north, and he has come”, with the verb of 41:2 (ASV “raised up”; JPS 1917 “roused up”; NJPS “roused”, checked). The north and *mimmizraḥ-šemeš* “the rising of the sun” together give the figure's direction. As at 41:2, the Hebrew names no one, and the line keeps lower case. *Yiqrāʾ ḇišmî* is “one who calls on my name” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “one who invokes My name”). A reading “he shall be called by name”, reported for 1QIsaᵃ and the LXX, was not verified.

*Wᵉyāḇōʾ sᵉḡānîm kᵉmô-ḥōmer* “and he shall come upon rulers as upon mortar” follows ASV and JPS 1917. NJPS has “And he has trampled rulers like mud” (checked), the sense given by the common emendation *wᵉyāḇōs* “and he shall trample”; NJPS gives no note here, so its basis was not verified. The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*Ḥōmer* is rendered by context in the book: the “mire” of the streets (10:6), the potter's “clay” (29:16; 45:9), and here “mortar”, the material trodden underfoot, as in ASV and JPS 1917 and as at Gen 11:3 in the corpus (“as mortar”). *Ṭîṭ* takes “clay”. *Kᵉmô yôṣēr* “as the potter” is the participle used on its own as a noun for the craftsman (overlay `yotser-potter-clay-image-isaiah`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`).

paragraphs.text: מִֽי־הִגִּ֤יד מֵרֹאשׁ֙ וְנֵדָ֔עָה וּמִלְּפָנִ֖ים וְנֹאמַ֣ר צַדִּ֑יק אַ֣ף אֵין־מַגִּ֗יד אַ֚ף אֵ֣ין מַשְׁמִ֔יעַ אַ֥ף אֵין־שֹׁמֵ֖עַ אִמְרֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Who declared it from the beginning, that we may know, and beforetime, that we may say, “He is right”? There is none who declares, yes, none who makes it heard, yes, none who hears your words.
i18n.he: מִֽי־הִגִּ֤יד מֵרֹאשׁ֙ וְנֵדָ֔עָה וּמִלְּפָנִ֖ים וְנֹאמַ֣ר צַדִּ֑יק אַ֣ף אֵין־מַגִּ֗יד אַ֚ף אֵ֣ין מַשְׁמִ֔יעַ אַ֥ף אֵין־שֹׁמֵ֖עַ אִמְרֵיכֶֽם׃

notes.official: *Wᵉnōʾmar ṣaddîq* “that we may say, ‘He is right’” follows ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS (checked). *Ṣaddîq* could also be neuter, “It is right”; cf. 43:9, where *ʾĕmeṯ* is “It is true”. *Mašmîaʿ* is “one who makes it heard”, as at 45:21 and 48:3 (ASV “showeth”; JPS 1917 “announceth”).

paragraphs.text: רִאשׁ֥וֹן לְצִיּ֖וֹן הִנֵּ֣ה הִנָּ֑ם וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מְבַשֵּׂ֥ר אֶתֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: I am the first to say to Zion, “Behold, behold them!” and to Jerusalem I give one who brings good tidings.
i18n.he: רִאשׁ֥וֹן לְצִיּ֖וֹן הִנֵּ֣ה הִנָּ֑ם וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מְבַשֵּׂ֥ר אֶתֵּֽן׃

notes.official: *Rišôn lᵉṣiyyôn hinnēh hinnām* is elliptical, and its meaning is uncertain. ASV supplies words in italics, “[I am the] first [that saith] unto Zion, Behold, behold them”, and the line follows ASV. JPS 1917 takes *rišôn* as a person, “A harbinger unto Zion will I give”. NJPS has “The things once predicted to Zion— Behold, here they are!”, with the note “Meaning of Heb. uncertain” (checked). Emendations have been proposed (not verified). *Mᵉḇaśśēr* is “one who brings good tidings”, as at 40:9 (*mᵉḇaśśereṯ*) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֙רֶא֙ וְאֵ֣ין אִ֔ישׁ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֵ֣ין יוֹעֵ֑ץ וְאֶשְׁאָלֵ֖ם וְיָשִׁ֥יבוּ דָבָֽר׃

i18n.en: And I look, and there is no one; and among these there is no counselor who, when I ask them, can answer a word.
i18n.he: וְאֵ֙רֶא֙ וְאֵ֣ין אִ֔ישׁ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֵ֣ין יוֹעֵ֑ץ וְאֶשְׁאָלֵ֖ם וְיָשִׁ֥יבוּ דָבָֽר׃

notes.official: *Wᵉʾên ʾîš* “and there is no one” (ASV and JPS 1917 “no man”; NJPS “not a man”, checked): generic *ʾîš* is rendered neutrally (overlay `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah`). *Yôʿēṣ* is “counselor”, and *wᵉyāšîḇû ḏāḇār* “can answer a word” (ASV).

paragraphs.text: הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם אָ֥וֶן אֶ֖פֶס מַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם ר֥וּחַ וָתֹ֖הוּ נִסְכֵּיהֶֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Behold, all of them — their works are vanity and nought; their molten images are wind and emptiness.
i18n.he: הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם אָ֥וֶן אֶ֖פֶס מַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם ר֥וּחַ וָתֹ֖הוּ נִסְכֵּיהֶֽם׃ (פ)

notes.official:
*Hēn kullām ʾāwen ʾep̄es maʿăśêhem* “Behold, all of them — their works are vanity and nought” follows the accents, with ASV and JPS 1917 (“Behold, all of them, their works are vanity and nought”). *ʾĀwen* is “iniquity” at its other sites in the book (1:13; 10:1; 29:20; 31:2; 32:6). Here, however, BDB lists the verse under the sense “idolatry … abstr. for concr. = idols” (Sefaria lexicon, checked), ASV and JPS 1917 have “vanity”, and NJPS has “nothingness” (checked). A reading *ʾayin* “nothing”, reported for 1QIsaᵃ, was not verified (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-41`; `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*Nᵉsāḵêhem* “their molten images” comes from *nsk* “pour, cast” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “Their statues”). The central `nesekh-libation-drink-offering` (“drink-offering”) is not applied to this sense. *Rûaḥ wāṯōhû* is “wind and emptiness” (overlay `tohu-bare-emptiness-wasteland-isaiah`; ASV and JPS 1917 “wind and confusion”).
